reason: Follows the existing rule C165 (rhombic = PATO:0001938 rhomboid); 'irregularly' is a degree word, not a different shape. Note that PATO defines rhomboid as a 3-D spheroid, so for flat lobes 'diamond shaped' (PATO_0002320) may be worth checking.
The bearer word 'margin' plus sinuate; FLOPO:0991113 is defined as a margin quality, so the value goes on the blade or petiole whose margin is meant.
'nearly'/'casi' is a qualifier of the existing value superior (sensu botany), the same as pattern 01; it should not be confused with half-inferior.

label: obturbinate
definition: A conical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like an inverted spinning top: broad and rounded at the proximal end and tapering to a narrow distal end. NOTE: The inverse of FLOPO:0991077 turbinate (under PATO:0002347 obconical).
reason: A standard term in Spanish and Neotropical floras for capsules and ovaries; it pairs with the existing turbinate class, and no PATO term has the rounded broad base.

reason: A compound of two shape values (square with rounded corners, in leaf cells of mosses and liverworts); it is a compound, not a new shape.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: spiny PATO_0001365 and warty PATO_0001361)
reason: A fruit surface with small warts bearing minute spines: two existing surface values combined.

target: new: position of greatest width (has position at plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023)
reason: It states where along the long axis the part is widest (as in Manual of Leaf Architecture character 10), across leaves, fruits and corollas. That is a position of a measure, not one shape term. Unlike the rejected 'broadest', the position is given.
Ash-coloured bark is grey (the colour table maps 'ashy gray' to FLOPO:0988010). The table maps 'ashen', 'ashy' and 'cendré' to blue (FLOPO:0988025), which looks wrong and should be checked.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: sagittate base and amplexicaul FLOPO:0991066)
reason: A leaf base that clasps the stem with backward-pointing auricles: an outline value plus an attachment value. Each part is annotated separately; neither alone covers the whole statement.
'sub-' is one of the four approximate qualifiers of pattern 01, applied to the existing glaucous.
Moss cells with a single nipple-like bulge are mammillose; 'bulging' only restates the protuberance in the mammillate definition.
Higher-order venation forming a network of small areoles is reticulate venation; the two halves say the same thing, and PATO_0002295 areolate is a ridge pattern on a surface.
Lacunae in the blades of aquatic plants (e.g. the lacunal bands of Potamogeton) are air spaces of aerenchyma. PO has no 'lacuna' class.

non-alate = not winged; alate is an EXACT synonym of PATO_0104354 winged.

A geofrutex (geoxyle) is a dwarf plant with a woody underground stem system and short-lived shoots, a kind of suffrutex. Suffrutescent habit is the nearest existing habit class, though narrower specialized terms are lost.

reason: 'Tinged with mauve' is a weak, approximate colour, like 'purplish'. Mauve already maps to purple in the colour table.
The staminal tube has no free rim beyond the anther insertions (Meliaceae). There is no PO part for the rim, and the phrase is a family-specific relation, not a general quality.
Chagriné = finely and evenly roughened like shagreen leather. PATO rough (synonym coarse) covers it without hairs or warts being implied.

reason: A compound of two outline values, as in 'oblong-ovate'.
A fine pubescence of gland-tipped hairs is what FLOPO:0991173 defines. The 'puberulous' degree can also be recorded as puberulous FLOPO:0991049 if wanted.
Suberified = turned into cork; corky has the related synonym suberose and the same bearers (bark, branches, seeds).
Half-orbicular calyx lobes and bracts are semicircular in outline. For a 3-D ovary or fruit, hemispheroid (PATO_0005000) is the matching reading.
Short stiff hairs = minutely hispid, which is what hispidulous means; this is better than splitting it into two values.

A leaf rolled into a tube, one margin wrapped over the other, is convolute. Involute (PATO_0001962) rolls both edges inwards and does not form a closed tube.
